definition: In any triangle, each side divided by the sine of the angle across from it gives the same value: $\frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B} = \frac{c}{\sin C}$; when it is used to find an angle, the angle may be acute or obtuse.
In any triangle, $a^{2} = b^{2} + c^{2} - 2bc\cos A$, which links all three sides to one angle; use it with two sides and the angle between them, or with three sides.
